MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 25, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:01 p.m., on June 25, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 20, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation; Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 2 cases

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  June 25, 2019
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered two Closed Session items with
three topics. The Council received updates and gave direction to staff but no reportable actions
occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Saddleback College Student Lexi Pound for her Design of the New Animal
  Services Logo

  Mayor Raths presented the certificate of recognition to Lexy Pound.

P2. Proclaim May through October, 2019, To Be "Drowning Prevention and Awareness"
  Months

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Fire Chief Capobianco..

P3. Featured Businesses of the Month - The Wisehart Lending Group and Coldwell Banker
  Residential Brokerage

  Mayor Raths presented proclamations to Nicolle Wisehart and Roy Fussell.

P4. Key to the City - Brightcare Veterinary Group

  Mayor Raths presented a key to the city to Dr. Ali Gorgi.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Adi Mitchell and Larry Garner, M.V.: announced that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee is
preparing for the 4th of July Street Fair which will be held on Olympiad Road beginning at 12:00
p.m. The event will conclude with a fireworks show at 9:00 p.m.

Justin Bass, M.V.: asked if the Council Members believe in global warming and climate change.
He stated that it is important that electric vehicle charging stations be available to residents and
that children should be taught about sustaining the planet.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed her dissatisfaction with the way that the City handled the Voting
Rights Act lawsuit and stated that the Council Members are rigging the upcoming election in their
favor.

Zachary Cadman, M.V.: announced that he is starting a new business in Mission Viejo, Adio
Chiropractic, in the Vista Paint Plaza at Alicia and Muirlands. Mr. Cadman said he expects to open
sometime in mid-September.

City Council Minutes  2  June 25, 2019
 Siavosh Zadeh, M.V.: thanked the City Council for helping his elderly neighbor resolve an issue
with overgrown trees in her yard.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 10 and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of June 11, 2019, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated May 31, 2019 in the Amount of $166,649.28

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated June 7, 2019 in the Amount of $940,383.66

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated June 14, 2019 in the Amount of $825,662.44

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Budget – Fiscal Year 2019/20

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 19-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority (MVHA) for FY 2019/20.

6.  FY 2019/20 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development Financing
  Authority

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 19-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2019/20 Fiscal Year.

7.  Establish an Appropriations Limit for the 2019-20 Fiscal Year

  Adopted Resolution 19-14 Establishing an Appropriations Limit for the 2019-20 Fiscal Year.

8.  Agreement for Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation Program - Theresa
  Dobbs dba Housing Rehabilitation Consulting Services (HRCS)
City Council Minutes  3  June 25, 2019
   Approved Agreement with HRCS (A19-36) from July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2021, in an amount
  not to exceed $115,900 ($57,950/year) for Technical Assistance.

9.  Microsoft Licensing Renewal

  Issued purchase order to SoftwareONE for year two of three-year Microsoft agreement for
  software licensing in the amount of $120,410.13 including a 3% contingency.

11. Olympiad Road/Felipe Road Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP
  18236)

  Authorized issuance of a purchase order to DKS Associates in an amount not to exceed
  $35,240 for design engineering services for Phase II (Operations & Maintenance) of Capital
  Improvement Project 18236.

12. Marguerite Parkway Median Island Shops Boulevard to Center Drive (CIP 239) –
  Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $31,135.88 thirty-
  five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion

13. Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP)

  Adopted Resolution 19-15 Ratifying the Submittal of Applications for Funds for the
  Environmental Cleanup, Tier 1 Grant Program under Orange County Local Transportation
  Ordinance No. 3 for the Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Projects.

15. Consultant Services to Produce, Direct and Cablecast Live City Council Meetings for
  Television and the Web

  (1) Awarded a contract for the subject services to Eric Winter (A19-37) for the period of July
  1, 2019, through June 30, 2021, in the amount of $38,907.00; and (2) authorized issuance of
  a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2020, in an
  amount not to exceed $18,711 pending adoption of the 2019- 2021 budget by the City
  Council.

16. Consultant Services for Coordination of Activities at Mission Viejo Television (MVTV)

  (1) Awarded a contract to Eric Winter (A19-38) for coordination of activities at Mission
  Viejo Television for the period of July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2021, in the amount of
  $51,373.56; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period
  of July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2020, in the amount of $25,395.72 pending adoption of the
  Fiscal Year 2019-2021 budget by the City Council.

City Council Minutes  4  June 25, 2019
 17. Consultant Services for Producer/Director of Various Mission Viejo Television
  Programs

  (1) Awarded a contract for the subject services to Eric Winter (A19-39) for the period of July
  1, 2019, through June 30, 2021, in the amount of $125,670.67; and (2) authorized issuance
  of a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2019, through June 30, 2020, in
  an amount not to exceed $62,847.33 pending adoption of the 2019- 2021 budget by the City
  Council.

18. Purchase of Pool Chemicals for Public Swimming Pools and Spas at City of Mission
  Viejo Recreation Centers

  (1) Approved the First Amendment to the existing contract (A17-50) with Waterline
  Technologies, Inc. for the period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2021 in the amount of $297,600;
  and; (2) issued a purchase order for the period of July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020 in an amount
  not to exceed $148,800 for the purchase of pool chemicals for the subject services.

19. Contract Amendment for Janitorial and Related Services for All City Facilities and
  Recreation Centers

  Approved Fourth Amendment to existing contract (A15-45) with Team One Management in
  an amount not to exceed $60,000 to cover current costs for janitorial and related services at
  City Facilities for the period of July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019.

20. Public Works Contract Inspection Services

  Approved proposal in an amount not to exceed $50,976 to CivilSource for the provision of
  contract inspection services.

21. Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Flashing Beacons,
  Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights and CCTV Cameras—Contract
  Extension

  Approved Second Amendment to Contract A15-54 with Computer Service Company, Inc.,
  extending the term of the contract to September 30, 2019.

22. Transfer Equipment to the County of Orange for the Electronic Ticket Writing System

  Approved the Transfer of Ownership of Three (3) Samsung Galaxy S9+ Cell Phones from
  the City of Mission Viejo to the County of Orange for the Electronic Ticket Writing System.

23. Technical Services Outsourcing for Mission Viejo Library

  Approved Agreement with Ingram Library Services, LLC (A19-40) for Customized Library
  Services in an amount not to exceed $200,000 per year for the provision of electronic
  selection lists, electronic ordering, acquisitions, cataloging, and physical processing of
  library materials, pending approval of the 2019-21 budget by the City Council.

City Council Minutes  5  June 25, 2019
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

10. Firewall Maintenance Renewal

  Council Member Sachs announced that he would have liked to have seen this agenda item a
  month earlier so the Council Members had time to pose questions and discuss the matter. He
  asked if there is an extension period allowed so the Council might have more time to review
  it and discuss outsourcing.

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander responded that firewall maintenance
  is not something that can be outsourced or placed in a cloud service; it needs to be on the
  City’s physical network.

  Council Member Sachs said it is imperative that the City look at opportunities for outsourcing
  security and other operations that are software-dependent.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve and issue purchase order for Cisco Firewall software subscription renewal to CDW-
  G in the amount of $53,578.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14. Update of Social Host Ordinance to Include Recreational Marijuana, Medical, Oils,
  Edible and Derivatives Provided to Underaged Individuals as Prohibited

  Council Member Sachs noted that he pulled this item from the Consent Calendar because he
  spoke against the ordinance at the last Council Meeting and he wished to register his no vote
  again. He said there is no reference to the data or conditions that require this ordinance and
  there are penal codes in place already that make these acts a misdemeanor. Council Member
  Sachs said the penalty under the penal code is greater than what is proposed in the ordinance.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Raths, to adopt Ordinance
  19-329 Amending the Title of Chapter 11.22 of Title 11 of The Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code and the definition of “Controlled Substances” in Section 11.22.010 of Chapter 11.22
  Of Title 11, as Amended Providing for Accountability for the Host of a Gathering Where
  Underage Drinking or Underage Marijuana Use Occurs, and/or Other Controlled Substances
  Are Consumed.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  June 25, 2019
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

24. General Plan Amendment GPA2018-32 / Zone Change ZC2018-21 / Planned
  Development Permit PDP2018-303 / Variance VAR2019-51 / and Tentative Tract Map
  TTM18187 - Petitions submitted by Shea Homes Limited Partnership to permit
  residential development on 6.73 acres of the total 10.3-acre Mission Foothill shopping
  center site located at 28715 Los Alisos Boulevard. GPA2018-32 is filed to change the
  subject site’s land use designation from Commercial Highway to Residential 30.
  ZC2018-21 is filed to change the site’s zoning from CH (Commercial Highway) and
  RPD30A (Residential Planned Development, Affordable) to RPD30 (Residential
  Planned Development). The proposed project includes demolition of 99,500 square feet
  of existing retail space to accommodate a new 105-dwelling-unit, for-sale project
  including 44 detached single-family units and 61 attached townhome units. All homes
  would be three stories with an overall project density of 15.6 du/ac. Four existing
  freestanding retail buildings, located adjacent to Los Alisos Boulevard, would remain,
  with the residential development occurring to the northeast, between the retail
  buildings and the SR 241 toll road

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the report.

  Larry Longenecker detailed the proposed project and shared images of the site plan,
  architectural style and building elevations.

  Bob Yoder and Brooke Doi, Shea Homes: outlined the proposed residential project at
  Mission Foothills Marketplace. They discussed their community outreach process and stated
  that they were met with mostly favorable feedback.

  Mayor Raths opened the public hearing at 7:08 p.m.

  The following expressed support for the proposed project: Lisa Dunn, M.V.; Jim Poettgen,
  M.V.; Chandy Andre, M.V.; Elizabeth Hansburg, People for Housing, Fullerton; Lacy
  Robertson, Local Government Affairs Committee Chair, Orange County Realtors
  Association, Laguna Hills; and Linda Tang, The Kennedy Commission, Irvine.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed opposition to the project as presented and requested that
  additional improvements that were requested at the Planning and Transportation Commission
  meeting be included.

  Mayor Raths closed the public hearing at 7:25 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  Adopt Resolution 19-16 Approving General Plan Amendment GPA2018-32 and Adopting
  the Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration Prepared for the Project; (2) introduce
  Ordinance 19-330 Approving Zone Change ZC2018-21, Being a Petition Submitted by Shea
  Homes Limited Partnership to Change the Zoning Map Designation from CH (Commercial
  Highway) and RPD30A (Residential Planned Development, Affordable) to RPD30
  (Residential Planned Development), for 6.73 Acres of the Property Located at 28715 Los
  Alisos Boulevard, Further Described as a Portion of Assessor Parcel Number 839-161-12;

City Council Minutes  7  June 25, 2019
   and (3) adopt Resolution 19-17 Approving Planned Development Permit PDP2018-303,
  Variance VAR2019-51, and Tentative Tract Map TTM18187.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

25. Recommended Name for the Wall of Recognition Display

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approved the addition of Cathy Allen to the Wall of Recognition Display.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

26. Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

27. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum announced that she had no report at this time.

28. Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2019 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

  Mayor Raths appointed Council Member Sachs as voting delegate and Mayor Pro Tem
  Goodell and Council Member Kelley to serve as alternates for the League of California Cities
  Conference Annual Business Meeting on October 18, 2019.

STAFF REPORTS

29. Adoption of the 2019-21 Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  8  June 25, 2019
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 19-18, as amended, Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for
  2019-21 and Appropriating Funds for the FY 2019/20 Only. Amendments: include the
  proposed adjustments for the 2020-21 expenditure budget as presented as Exhibit A to the
  staff report, with the exception of (1) closure of the Sierra Recreation Center from 1-3 p.m.
  during a 9-month period, and (2) open lap swim at Marguerite Aquatics Complex which will
  be accommodated with Recreation Centers membership or the purchase of a punch pass.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

30. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum commended the Chamber of Commerce and Mayor Raths for a nice
and succinct presentation at the Chamber’s State of the City breakfast. She said it was a great event
and the business highlights really demonstrated the economic development activity that has been
going on in Mission Viejo. She also outlined her attendance at the Swim Meet of Champions where
she was proud to hear her husband sing the National Anthem and see the people enjoying the City's
aquatics facility. Council Member Bucknum noted that several Nadadores swimmers placed in the
meet, there were Olympians present, and new records set. She thanked the Nadadores for putting
on a great event and inviting the Council Members to present awards. Council Member Bucknum
stated that she looks forward to seeing everyone at the 4th of July Street Faire and she encouraged
residents to buy fundraiser raffle tickets at the event.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the Fran Crippen Swim Meet of Champions
and stated that she was struck by the number of people that came by to thank her for the updated
aquatics facility. She also outlined her attendance at the recent South Orange County Amateur
Radio Association (SOARA) Field Day at Gilleran Park. It was an educational experience and the
radio operations are an important part of the City’s emergency preparedness efforts. Council
Member Kelley thanked members of the Mission Viejo Radio Amateur Civil Emergency Service
(RACES) team and SOARA for all that they do. In conclusion, she reminded residents that the
Marine Adoption Committee’s Boots Beer & BBQ event will be held July 21, 2019, from 4:00 to
7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. Council Member Kelley said that attending the event
is one way to help the City’s adopted Marines and tickets can be purchased at the Community
Center or online at mvcommunityfoundation.org.

City Council Minutes  9  June 25, 2019
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he was touched earlier in the meeting to hear one of the
public speakers comment about the City pulling resources together to help an elderly woman
manage her yard. He said that is the kind of thing that really makes him proud to be part of this
community. He also complimented the Planning and Transportation Commissioners for the work
they did on the Shea Homes project. He shared that all of the City’s Commissioners do a lot of
pre-work to take the load off the Council and he thanked them for their dedication and diligence.
Council Member Sachs announced that he had three private meetings at the recent energy
symposium and it was enlightening to learn what other energy options cities and communities
have. He said it’s important that the City look into this because the Public Utilities Commission
turned down SDG&E’s request to eliminate a higher-usage charge for electric bills which means
that the $1,000 monthly utility bill is looming for many as the summer months heat up. He noted
that there is another price increase coming for San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E) customers
which will make SDG&E the most expensive utility in the United States. Council Member Sachs
said that fire suppression needs to be looked at and he is trying to coordinate a fall Town Hall
meeting with the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) so residents can get answers and
ask questions of CPUC staff.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that he attended the Community of Character gala which
honored graduating seniors and incoming new members and it was wonderful to see young people
embracing the ideals of the committee. He also attended the YMCA’s Volunteer and Community
Partner Distinguished Service Luncheon where Kristen Moore was honored for heading up a
program that supports Mission Viejo students in the Model United Nations program. He outlined
his attendance at other events including the Chamber of Commerce State of the City breakfast and
the Fran Crippen Swim Meet of Champions which had more than 1,400 swimmers and at least
5,000 in attendance. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell said that it is so great to see that Marguerite Aquatics
Center really shine. He also noted that the Olympic Promotion Committee is meeting tomorrow
and they are doing very well with current events and planning ahead for future events. He shared
that he is really excited about the completion of the new Saddleback College stadium and stated
that there should be a real uptick in the quality and number of sporting events in Mission Viejo
when it is done. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell said the City will need more hotel rooms and a possible
increase in the Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) with all of the sporting events occurring in town.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths asked the City Manager to place mid-year reports from the Sheriff’s Department and
the Fire Authority on the next Council meeting agenda. He thanked resident and nurse Anna T.
Boyce for helping with yesterday’s blood drive which resulted in 34 pints of donated blood. Mayor
Raths congratulated resident Cathy Allen for being nominated and approved for the wall of
recognition at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. He also outlined his attendance at recent
events including an open house for the new South Orange County Veterans Center and the Mission
Viejo Character Committee gala. Mayor Raths expressed his thanks to Council Member Kelley
for everything she does for the Character Committee. He also announced that he was just elected
Vice Chair for the Orange County Veterans Advisory Council and he thanked the Chamber of
Commerce for a great job on the State of the City breakfast. He concluded by complimenting the

City Council Minutes  10  June 25, 2019
 Nadadores on a great Swim Meet of Champions and he noted that the scoreboard was especially
impressive.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:05 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 9, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 9, 2019

City Council Minutes  11  June 25, 2019
